summary: In international launch developments, a Chinese Long March 7A rocket exploded less than 90 seconds after liftoff, marking a major setback for the nation's space program, while Japan successfully delivered a 10,800-pound navigation satellite to high Earth orbit aboard an H3 rocket and tank issues delayed the maiden launch of Rocket Factory Augsburg. On the commercial front, Rocket Lab unveiled its "GHOST" mobile spaceport system for Electron launches and secured a 2028 Neutron launch agreement with Kepler Communications, as Europe’s IRIS2 satellite constellation formally entered its build phase and MDA Space announced plans to repurpose Canadarm3 technology for the lunar surface. In civil space and scientific research, the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument project released the largest two-dimensional map of the universe created to date, NASA's James Webb Space Telescope identified a new object from the early universe, and engineers at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory successfully restored functionality to a distant Voyager spacecraft. In military and defense policy, a U.S. Senate bill temporarily blocked proposed federal science funding cuts, the Pentagon revoked the security clearance of former Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall, and the U.S. Air Force began seeking artificial intelligence tools to support Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile sustainment. Skywatchers and scientists alike should look ahead to the total solar eclipse set to cross the globe on August 12, 2026.
